Who they are: Solo writers and producers in a DAW most evenings. Own an interface, maybe a controller.
What the button solves for them: One press arms record, drops a marker, or taps tempo without leaving the take. The light is a tally you can see from the vocal booth.
Why that score: Deepest working feature set already (MIDI, OSC, MCU feedback, tempo follow) and a buyer who already spends on desk hardware. Proof exists; only the story is missing.
Further considerations: Needs a per-DAW setup path, not a MIDI-learn maze. Ableton/Studio One/Logic each want their own scene. The DAW rig test (TODO 77) has never run on real hardware.
Gap idea 1 (not in the button today): A punch-in/out app that reads the DAW's loop points back
Gap idea 2: Take counter that names each take in the DAW
Gap idea 3: A metronome that flashes the count-in and then gets out of the way

Who they are: Playing out. Backing tracks, patch changes, in-ear cues.
What the button solves for them: A hand- or foot-reachable cue that changes patch, starts a track, or flashes the next section to the band.
Why that score: Real money and real pain, but stage reliability is a hardware promise the current build cannot make (no enclosure, BLE only, no battery story).
Further considerations: Latency and dropout are pass/fail on stage, not annoyances. Needs the standalone path (TODO 111) proven before it can be sold here.
Gap idea 1 (not in the button today): Setlist app: one press advances the song, the light shows the next key
Gap idea 2: Silent cue to the drummer - a second button that only flashes
Gap idea 3: Panic button that kills the backing track

Who they are: Twitch/YouTube/TikTok. OBS, alerts, a busy desk, an audience that sees the desk.
What the button solves for them: One press toggles scene, mute, or the on-air light. The LED is the on-air light, and it is on camera.
Why that score: Highest here: the product is visible in every frame, the audience is the ad, and webhook support exists already. A creator button is a category people already buy.
Further considerations: Deck-style competitors are entrenched and cheap; the wedge is the light being a prop, not the macro count. OBS websocket should be a first-class action, not a webhook.
Gap idea 1 (not in the button today): Native OBS websocket action (scene, mute, replay buffer)
Gap idea 2: Chat-triggered reflex - light reacts to subs/donations
Gap idea 3: A follower/goal readout rendered on the LED, not a screen

Who they are: Keyboard-and-mouse, Discord, macros, a lit desk.
What the button solves for them: A physical push-to-talk, a macro key outside the keyboard, and a light that means something in-game.
Why that score: Big, reachable, spends on peripherals. HID keys already ship. The multi-button ideas (TODO 116) land hardest here.
Further considerations: Anti-cheat blocks anything resembling input automation in some titles - check before promising macros. Latency budget matters.
Gap idea 1 (not in the button today): Game-state reflex: health/cooldown drives the light via a game API
Gap idea 2: A push-to-talk that shows mute state without alt-tabbing
Gap idea 3: Multi-button macro pad with apps unlocked at N (TODO 116)

Who they are: Weekly game night, prints their own handouts, buys dice they do not need.
What the button solves for them: A table-side prop that sets the mood light, tracks initiative, and rolls a hidden result.
Why that score: Small but ferociously spendy and community-driven. The button reads as an artefact at the table, which is the whole sale.
Further considerations: Hobby buys travel by word of mouth, not ads - seed to DMs, not to a demographic. Needs the light library (TODO 113) for mood presets to be worth anything.
Gap idea 1 (not in the button today): Initiative tracker: a press advances the turn, the light names whose it is
Gap idea 2: Hidden dice roll - the light tells only the GM the result
Gap idea 3: Scene mood presets a player can trigger from across the table

Who they are: Soldering iron on the desk, an ESP32 in a drawer, reads the schematic before the manual.
What the button solves for them: An open scriptable reflashable button that does not hide anything.
Why that score: Closest to who this was built for. They forgive rough edges, write the missing integrations, and become the app bank.
Further considerations: They will not pay a premium for a closed product - open firmware and a documented protocol are the offer. Undercut risk is real: they can build one for parts cost, so the value has to be the software.
Gap idea 1 (not in the button today): A scripting/expression layer in the app runtime (already on the roadmap)
Gap idea 2: GPIO/expansion header so the button drives their own hardware
Gap idea 3: Community app packages - install someone else's .pkg over BLE

Who they are: CI, PRs, pagers, a terminal that never closes.
What the button solves for them: A build light and a one-press acknowledge. The LED is a CI status you cannot tab away from.
Why that score: Genuine everyday utility and an easy demo, but this crowd builds rather than buys and the budget is personal, not company.
Further considerations: Corporate MDM makes BLE dongles and background services awkward on work laptops. Webhook polling (TODO 99) is the enabling piece.
Gap idea 1 (not in the button today): Poll a CI/PR endpoint and render the state (TODO 99/100)
Gap idea 2: Acknowledge a page with one press, escalate on long press
Gap idea 3: A focus/interrupt light your team can see in a shared office

Who they are: Calls all day, a home office door people walk through.
What the button solves for them: A do-not-disturb light with one press, and a mute key that is not buried in a window.
Why that score: Enormous market, obvious use, but crowded by cheap busy-lights. The button wins by also being everything else.
Further considerations: Calendar and meeting-state integration is the difference between a light and a toy - and that needs the secret store (TODO 96) first.
Gap idea 1 (not in the button today): Calendar-driven light: turns red on its own when a meeting starts
Gap idea 2: Global mute for Zoom/Teams/Meet with state shown on the LED
Gap idea 3: A household-visible signal: one button on the desk, one on the door

Who they are: Time-blind, task-switch cost is real, hates apps that nag from a screen.
What the button solves for them: An off-screen single-purpose object: start a timer with one press, see time passing as light instead of numbers.
Why that score: High intent, high word-of-mouth, and the core strength (physical, off-screen, one decision) is exactly the accommodation. Pomodoro and countdown already ship.
Further considerations: Sell as a tool, not a treatment - avoid medical claims entirely. This community is sensitive to being marketed at.
Gap idea 1 (not in the button today): A visual time-remaining ramp anyone can read across a room
Gap idea 2: A body-double / co-working session light shared with a friend
Gap idea 3: Task capture: press to log 'I switched' without opening anything

Who they are: Bedtime routines, chore charts, a household that ignores reminders.
What the button solves for them: A kid-legible signal that is not a screen: green means go, red means bed.
Why that score: Real recurring pain and an easy story, but price sensitivity is high and durability matters more than features.
Further considerations: Anything a child touches needs an enclosure and a safety story. Multi-button (TODO 116) is what makes the household version work.
Gap idea 1 (not in the button today): Routine app: a sequence of steps a child taps through
Gap idea 2: A quiet-hours reflex - the light changes when the house should be calm
Gap idea 3: A chore chart the counter's readout already almost is

Who they are: Loves buttons, breaks things, cannot read a config screen.
What the button solves for them: A toy that responds instantly, and games that need nothing but the button.
Why that score: Delightful demo, hard business. Toy safety, durability and parental setup all cost more than the software.
Further considerations: Toy-grade compliance is a real barrier for a small run. Best sold as a parent-configured mode of the household button, not a separate SKU.
Gap idea 1 (not in the button today): A simple colour-matching or memory game (extends hotcold/reaction)
Gap idea 2: Sticker/reward tally with a celebration light
Gap idea 3: A 'read to me' pacing light for practice reading

Who they are: 30 kids, a noise level, a timer that has to be visible from the back.
What the button solves for them: A room-visible timer and a turn signal that does not need the projector.
Why that score: Clear use and enthusiastic early adopters, but school purchasing is slow and per-unit budget is near zero.
Further considerations: Sell to the teacher personally, not the district. Needs to be visible at 10 m, which one small LED may simply not be - test before promising.
Gap idea 1 (not in the button today): Turn-taking token: the light names who has the floor
Gap idea 2: A group timer several buttons share (TODO 116)
Gap idea 3: Noise-level reflex driven by the PC's microphone

Who they are: Intervals, sets, rest timers, a phone they would rather not touch mid-set.
What the button solves for them: A sweaty-hands-proof interval timer that shows work/rest as colour.
Why that score: The interval app exists and Tabata/HIIT presets ship, but phones and watches own this space and do it well.
Further considerations: Needs to survive a gym bag and be readable in daylight - both hardware questions. Probably a feature that sells other archetypes, not a segment of its own.
Gap idea 1 (not in the button today): Rep counter driven by a press per set, with a rest light
Gap idea 2: A round timer a coach triggers for a whole class
Gap idea 3: Heart-rate-zone light from a paired strap

Who they are: Season ticket, team colours, watch parties, a stadium full of people who all bought a thing.
What the button solves for them: Team colours on a physical object - and eventually a whole stand lighting up together.
Why that score: The single biggest upside idea in the pile (crowd sync, TODO 115) and the best possible ad, but it is the furthest from shipping.
Further considerations: Team names are trademarks - the light library must ship colours and tags, not club names (TODO 113). Stadium deals are a different business to selling one button.
Gap idea 1 (not in the button today): Crowd sync: coordinated colour across a stand (TODO 115)
Gap idea 2: Goal/score reflex from a live sports API
Gap idea 3: A team look pack in the light library, searchable by city

Who they are: Site work, gloves, dust, a phone in a case that has already been dropped.
What the button solves for them: Honestly: very little a rugged phone or a shop timer does not already do.
Why that score: Lowest-fit segment in this list. The button is a desk object with a delicate LED and a BLE dependency on a PC that is not on site.
Further considerations: Worth writing down as a deliberate no. If it is ever revisited it is a different physical product, not a scene.
Gap idea 1 (not in the button today): A site-safe standalone timer with no host at all
Gap idea 2: Loud audible alarm - the buzzer is nowhere near enough for a job site
Gap idea 3: A wearable or mountable form factor

Who they are: Shelf of figures, deep in one franchise, buys the thing because it is the thing.
What the button solves for them: A shelf object that shows a franchise's colours and reacts when something happens.
Why that score: Very high, and it is the light library's payoff: thousands of palettes people search their fandom for is exactly the browse-and-buy loop.
Further considerations: Same trademark caution as sports. Community-authored palettes sidestep most of it - decide the policy once (TODO 113).
Gap idea 1 (not in the button today): Franchise palette packs, searchable, in the light library
Gap idea 2: A 'countdown to release' shelf light
Gap idea 3: Ambient reactive mode driven by what is playing on the PC

Who they are: Concerts, festivals, cons. Owns the light-up wristband from the last tour.
What the button solves for them: A wristband you own, that you configured, that works at the next show too.
Why that score: Proven behaviour - tours already hand these out - and it upgrades a disposable into a keepsake. Needs crowd sync to be more than a colour.
Further considerations: The tour-issued version is free to the fan and paid by the promoter; that is a B2B motion, not a consumer one. Two businesses in one idea.
Gap idea 1 (not in the button today): Crowd sync at a venue with a join code (TODO 115)
Gap idea 2: A show mode that reacts to the PC's audio when at home
Gap idea 3: Buttons as pixels of an image across a crowd (TODO 115)

Who they are: Marches, mutual aid, distrust of platforms and cloud accounts.
What the button solves for them: A signal that works with no account, and a light that says one thing loudly.
Why that score: Strong emotional fit with the open/offline story, but a small, non-spending and reputationally complicated segment.
Further considerations: Anything sold as protest kit invites scrutiny of the crowd features and of what the sync server logs. Offline-first is the honest offer; do not build tracking into it.
Gap idea 1 (not in the button today): Fully offline device-to-device signalling - no host, no server
Gap idea 2: A silent mode - buzzer only, no light
Gap idea 3: Pre-written signal codes on a printed card (see TODO 112)

Who they are: Wants one small ritual to stick. Water, meds, stretch, journal.
What the button solves for them: A press that records a thing happened, and a light that shows the streak.
Why that score: Broad and shallow. Counter, readout and notices already do it; the problem is that habit apps are free and everywhere.
Further considerations: The differentiator is that it is on the desk and not in a phone - lead with that, not with features. Retention is weak without a readout people love.
Gap idea 1 (not in the button today): A streak light that is genuinely satisfying to keep alive
Gap idea 2: Medication reminder with an acknowledged/missed record (TODO 84b)
Gap idea 3: Mood check-in: press a colour, get a chart

Who they are: Home Assistant, MQTT, a dashboard nobody else in the house uses.
What the button solves for them: A physical control their household will actually press wired into what they already built.
Why that score: Technically sophisticated, already spending, and the webhook action nearly serves them today. Good multiplier: they build the integrations.
Further considerations: Home Assistant users expect local control and no cloud - a BLE-to-PC hop is a weakness. An ESPHome/MQTT path may matter more than any app.
Gap idea 1 (not in the button today): Native MQTT / Home Assistant action, local, no host service
Gap idea 2: A light that mirrors home state (door open, laundry done)
Gap idea 3: Direct Wi-Fi mode so the button needs no PC at all

Who they are: Sets, tally lights, a director who needs to know when to talk.
What the button solves for them: A recording tally and a silent cue between crew.
Why that score: Narrow, and the professional versions are cheap, wired and trusted. The amateur end overlaps streamers, who score much higher.
Further considerations: Sell into this only through the streamer story. Wireless tally is a solved problem with known-good hardware.
Gap idea 1 (not in the button today): Camera tally over a second button (TODO 116)
Gap idea 2: A silent countdown cue for talent
Gap idea 3: Timecode / slate marker on press

Who they are: Deaf and hard-of-hearing households, carers, memory support.
What the button solves for them: A light that carries information sound normally would - doorbell, alarm, timer, prompt.
Why that score: Genuinely valuable and underserved, and the light-first design suits it. Scored down because the sales motion is care organisations and the reliability bar is high.
Further considerations: This crosses into 'someone depends on it', which is a different standard of testing and a different liability. Not a casual scene.
Gap idea 1 (not in the button today): Sound-to-light reflex: doorbell / alarm / name detection on the PC
Gap idea 2: A one-press check-in a family member sees remotely
Gap idea 3: High-contrast plain-language look set with no strobing at all

Who they are: Front of house, back of house, a bell and a shout.
What the button solves for them: A quiet call button between counter and kitchen.
Why that score: Real problem, but commercial paging systems own it and per-site purchasing is slow. The button is not built for a shift.
Further considerations: Needs multi-button (TODO 116) plus reliability nobody has tested. Probably not worth a scene until that exists.
Gap idea 1 (not in the button today): Pager: press here, buzz there (TODO 116)
Gap idea 2: A queue counter with a shared readout
Gap idea 3: Shift timer nobody has to look at a screen to read

Who they are: Builds the prop, wires the LEDs, wants a control that hides inside it.
What the button solves for them: A tiny configurable light-and-trigger core they can embed.
Why that score: Passionate, visible, and shares everything they make - excellent organic reach for a small segment.
Further considerations: They will want the board bare and the enclosure gone; that is a component sale, not a product sale. The light library and open firmware are the draw.
Gap idea 1 (not in the button today): A bare-board / embed variant with a JST light output
Gap idea 2: Per-pixel ring support so a prop can have a strip (TODO 52b)
Gap idea 3: Trigger patterns for a prop: charge-up, fire, cooldown

Who they are: Clicker training, feeding schedules, a dog that hears the treat bag.
What the button solves for them: A clicker that also keeps count, and a feeding light the household shares.
Why that score: Charming and demo-friendly, but the clicker is three dollars and works. The value is the record-keeping, which is a screen problem.
Further considerations: Buzzer sound quality matters here in a way it does not elsewhere - a clicker has a specific sharp sound.
Gap idea 1 (not in the button today): Training-session recorder: press per success, get a session chart
Gap idea 2: Feeding light - nobody double-feeds the dog
Gap idea 3: A timed 'stay' with a light the dog can be trained on

Who they are: Runs a timeline, cues a DJ, keeps a room moving.
What the button solves for them: A discreet cue between planner, DJ and photographer.
Why that score: Small, seasonal and service-led. It is a rental business more than a product one.
Further considerations: Would need several buttons, a charge story and setup by someone who is not technical. Furthest from the current shape.
Gap idea 1 (not in the button today): Cue chain across roles (TODO 116)
Gap idea 2: Timeline app: next event, time remaining, at a glance
Gap idea 3: Guest-facing colour moments across the room (TODO 115)

Who they are: Runs classes, calls intervals, watches a clock more than the class.
What the button solves for them: A class-visible work/rest light so nobody has to hear the call.
Why that score: The interval app is done, so this is nearly free content - but gyms already have wall clocks and apps that project.
Further considerations: Best treated as a scene shipping alongside the athlete one rather than a segment of its own. Visibility at distance is the open question.
Gap idea 1 (not in the button today): Class-wide sync so every member's button shows the round
Gap idea 2: A programmable ladder of rounds with named blocks
Gap idea 3: Coach override: skip or extend the round from one press

Who they are: Anyone with a computer and a desk. No single identity - wants one object that does several small things well.
What the button solves for them: One button, four gestures, doing the four things they do all day: focus timer, mute, do-not-disturb, shortcut.
Why that score: The honest default scene and the one most first buyers actually live in. Sells the product rather than a niche, and it is what the ambient layer already is.
Further considerations: Risk is blandness - a generalist scene has to be configured well, not merely populated. This is the scene to spend the most authoring effort on.
Gap idea 1 (not in the button today): A guided first run that asks four questions and writes the scene
Gap idea 2: Profile switching by time of day, not by press
Gap idea 3: Usage readout that suggests what to bind to the unused gesture

Who they are: A family, one button in a shared space, several people who will press it.
What the button solves for them: Shared signals: dinner is ready, quiet hours, laundry is done, someone is on a call.
Why that score: Strong story and the clearest reason to own more than one, but it depends almost entirely on multi-button work that does not exist yet.
Further considerations: Needs to work with no PC awake, which is standalone (TODO 111) plus a mesh (TODO 116). Do not write this scene before those land.
Gap idea 1 (not in the button today): Broadcast: one press changes every button in the house
Gap idea 2: A shared state anyone in the house can clear
Gap idea 3: Per-person colour so the signal says who sent it

Who they are: Music and streaming and presenting from the same desk - the overlap archetype.
What the button solves for them: A single scene covering record, on-air, mute and cue, switching by context instead of by mode.
Why that score: Real people live here (the owner does), but it is a power-user scene that assumes a configured machine. Good documentation piece, weak advertisement.
Further considerations: This is the scene that will expose every rough edge in scene metadata and missing-integration warnings - write it early for that reason, not for sales.
Gap idea 1 (not in the button today): Context switching driven by which app has focus on the PC
Gap idea 2: A single 'go live' chain that touches DAW, OBS and the light
Gap idea 3: Per-scene readout so you can see what the rig did today
